observation.visible_scene: A close, slightly angled view of a weathered wooden plank surface (decking or table) made of horizontal boards separated by dark gaps. A single dark oval hole/knot sits in one of the upper boards. Faded, mottled discoloration and damp-looking stains cover the grain. A fixed text watermark (Chinese characters plus 'LIFE FOREST LIFE') is overlaid in the lower-right corner throughout. No people, tools, or moving objects are present.
visible_changes: The camera drifts very slowly: the oval hole and the plank gap lines shift only a few pixels upward and leftward over the excerpt, moving together as one rigid pattern, indicating small camera translation/pan rather than any object moving across the surface.

Dappled light and shadow patches on the wood brighten and shift subtly from frame to frame (e.g., the upper-left area and the bright band near the top change intensity), consistent with moving sunlight or a slight change in viewing angle.
The lower-right watermark stays locked to the screen edges, confirming it is an overlay and not part of the physical scene.
The dark stains and the oval hole keep constant positions relative to the boards, so they are fixed surface features, not moving entities.
outside_clip_unknowns: What lies beyond the cropped deck area and whether the camera continues to pan after the last frame.
The cause of the shifting light (clouds, foliage, or camera angle) and the origin of the oval hole.
uncertain_details: The exact direction and magnitude of the camera motion are small and gradual; it reads as a slow drift rather than a deliberate pan.
It is not fully certain whether the brightness changes come from moving light patterns or from the slight camera repositioning.
